claim: The nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex is asymmetrically segregated into the surviving daughter cell rather than the apoptotic one during asymmetric cell divisions in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex is asymmetrically segregated into the surviving daughter cell rather than the apoptotic one during ACDs in Caenorhabditis elegans.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing fluorescence imaging of NuRD components in dividing cells, as described in the abstract and demonstrated in the figures.

claim: The absence of NuRD triggers apoptosis via the EGL-1-CED-9-CED-4-CED-3 pathway.
source: The absence of NuRD triggers apoptosis via the EGL-1-CED-9-CED-4-CED-3 pathway, while an ectopic gain of NuRD enables apoptotic daughter cells to survive.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that RNAi of NuRD components increases apoptosis in a manner dependent on the canonical apoptosis pathway components.

claim: An ectopic gain of NuRD enables apoptotic daughter cells to survive.
source: The absence of NuRD triggers apoptosis via the EGL-1-CED-9-CED-4-CED-3 pathway, while an ectopic gain of NuRD enables apoptotic daughter cells to survive.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that BafA1 treatment, which causes ectopic NuRD in apoptotic cells, allows them to survive.

claim: The vacuolar H+–adenosine triphosphatase (V-ATPase) complex is a crucial regulator of NuRD's asymmetric segregation.
source: We identify the vacuolar H+–adenosine triphosphatase (V-ATPase) complex as a crucial regulator of NuRD's asymmetric segregation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that V-ATPase interacts with NuRD and that inhibition of V-ATPase disrupts NuRD asymmetry.

claim: V-ATPase interacts with NuRD.
source: V-ATPase interacts with NuRD and is asymmetrically segregated into the surviving daughter cell.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry data identifying V-ATPase subunits as binding partners of HDA-1.

claim: V-ATPase is asymmetrically segregated into the surviving daughter cell.
source: V-ATPase interacts with NuRD and is asymmetrically segregated into the surviving daughter cell.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data showing VHA-17 enrichment in the surviving daughter cell.

claim: Inhibition of V-ATPase disrupts cytosolic pH asymmetry.
source: Inhibition of V-ATPase disrupts cytosolic pH asymmetry and NuRD asymmetry.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using pHluorin reporter showing reduced pH asymmetry upon BafA1 treatment.

claim: Inhibition of V-ATPase disrupts NuRD asymmetry.
source: Inhibition of V-ATPase disrupts cytosolic pH asymmetry and NuRD asymmetry.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing symmetric HDA-1 distribution upon BafA1 treatment.

claim: Asymmetric segregation of V-ATPase may cause distinct acidification levels in the two daughter cells.
source: We suggest that asymmetric segregation of V-ATPase may cause distinct acidification levels in the two daughter cells, enabling asymmetric epigenetic inheritance that specifies their respective life-versus-death fates.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from the observed pH asymmetry and V-ATPase distribution.

claim: Asymmetric epigenetic inheritance specifies life-versus-death fates of daughter cells.
source: We suggest that asymmetric segregation of V-ATPase may cause distinct acidification levels in the two daughter cells, enabling asymmetric epigenetic inheritance that specifies their respective life-versus-death fates.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing NuRD's role in suppressing apoptosis and its asymmetric distribution.

claim: Asymmetric cell division gives rise to two daughter cells that possess identical genetic material but distinct cell fates.
source: Asymmetric cell division (ACD) gives rise to two daughter cells that possess identical genetic material but distinct cell fates, playing a crucial role in both development and tissue homeostasis (Royall and Jessberger, 2021; Sunchu and Cabernard, 2020; Venkei and Yamashita, 2018; Wooten et al., 2020; Zion et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature on asymmetric cell division.

claim: Asymmetric cell division plays a crucial role in both development and tissue homeostasis.
source: Asymmetric cell division (ACD) gives rise to two daughter cells that possess identical genetic material but distinct cell fates, playing a crucial role in both development and tissue homeostasis (Royall and Jessberger, 2021; Sunchu and Cabernard, 2020; Venkei and Yamashita, 2018; Wooten et al., 2020; Zion et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Both extrinsic and intrinsic mechanisms determine distinct daughter cell fates after ACD.
source: Both extrinsic and intrinsic mechanisms determine distinct daughter cell fates after ACD.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge in the field of cell biology.

claim: Extrinsic mechanisms, such as exposure to signaling cues from the local niche, have been extensively studied and are known to define stem cell fate.
source: While extrinsic mechanisms, such as exposure to signaling cues from the local niche, have been extensively studied and are known to define stem cell fate (Morrison and Spradling, 2008), the intrinsic mechanisms are more complex and largely unresolved, despite several proteins, RNA molecules, and organelles having been implicated in the regulation of some types of ACD (Sunchu and Cabernard, 2020; Zion et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Morrison and Spradling, 2008.

claim: Intrinsic mechanisms of asymmetric cell division are more complex and largely unresolved.
source: While extrinsic mechanisms, such as exposure to signaling cues from the local niche, have been extensively studied and are known to define stem cell fate (Morrison and Spradling, 2008), the intrinsic mechanisms are more complex and largely unresolved, despite several proteins, RNA molecules, and organelles having been implicated in the regulation of some types of ACD (Sunchu and Cabernard, 2020; Zion et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations indicating the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Several proteins, RNA molecules, and organelles have been implicated in the regulation of some types of ACD.
source: While extrinsic mechanisms, such as exposure to signaling cues from the local niche, have been extensively studied and are known to define stem cell fate (Morrison and Spradling, 2008), the intrinsic mechanisms are more complex and largely unresolved, despite several proteins, RNA molecules, and organelles having been implicated in the regulation of some types of ACD (Sunchu and Cabernard, 2020; Zion et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sunchu and Cabernard, 2020; Zion et al., 2020.

claim: Epigenetic mechanisms play a crucial role in guiding the two daughter cells toward establishing differential gene expression profiles.
source: Epigenetic mechanisms play a crucial role in guiding the two daughter cells toward establishing differential gene expression profiles, ultimately defining their unique cell identities (Allis and Jenuwein, 2016; Escobar et al., 2021; Stewart-Morgan et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Allis and Jenuwein, 2016; Escobar et al., 2021; Stewart-Morgan et al., 2020.

claim: During the ACD of Drosophila male germline stem cells, pre-existing and newly synthesized histones H3 and H4 are asymmetrically segregated toward the stem daughter cell and the differentiating daughter cell, respectively.
source: During the ACD of Drosophila male germline stem cells (GSCs), pre-existing and newly synthesized histones H3 and H4 are asymmetrically segregated toward the stem daughter cell and the differentiating daughter cell, respectively (Wooten et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wooten et al., 2020.

claim: The extent to which epigenetic information is asymmetrically inherited through ACD in other organisms and the mechanism by which this process occurs remains elusive.
source: Nevertheless, the extent to which epigenetic information is asymmetrically inherited through ACD in other organisms and the mechanism by which this process occurs remains elusive.
evidence: This claim represents a knowledge gap in the field, based on the authors' assessment of the literature.

claim: Caenorhabditis elegans represents a valuable model for investigating ACD, given its invariant cell lineage and conserved mechanisms of ACD.
source: Caenorhabditis elegans represents a valuable model for investigating ACD, given its invariant cell lineage and conserved mechanisms of ACD.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about C. elegans as a model organism.

claim: During hermaphrodite development in C. elegans, 131 somatic cells undergo programmed cell death.
source: During hermaphrodite development in C. elegans, 131 somatic cells undergo programmed cell death, with the majority produced through ACD that create a large cell programmed for survival and a small cell programmed to die (Sulston and Horvitz, 1977; Sulston et al., 1983)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sulston and Horvitz, 1977; Sulston et al., 1983.

claim: The majority of apoptotic cells in C. elegans are produced through ACD that create a large cell programmed for survival and a small cell programmed to die.
source: During hermaphrodite development in C. elegans, 131 somatic cells undergo programmed cell death, with the majority produced through ACD that create a large cell programmed for survival and a small cell programmed to die (Sulston and Horvitz, 1977; Sulston et al., 1983)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sulston and Horvitz, 1977; Sulston et al., 1983.

claim: 105 of the 131 apoptotic cells in C. elegans arise from neuronal lineages.
source: It is noteworthy that 105 of the 131 apoptotic cells arise from neuronal lineages, of which the Q neuroblast represents a tractable system for studying ACD and apoptosis at single-cell resolution (Ellis and Horvitz, 1986; Hedgecock et al., 1983; Ou et al., 2010; Sulston and Horvitz, 1977).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ellis and Horvitz, 1986; Hedgecock et al., 1983; Ou et al., 2010; Sulston and Horvitz, 1977.

claim: The Q neuroblast represents a tractable system for studying ACD and apoptosis at single-cell resolution.
source: It is noteworthy that 105 of the 131 apoptotic cells arise from neuronal lineages, of which the Q neuroblast represents a tractable system for studying ACD and apoptosis at single-cell resolution (Ellis and Horvitz, 1986; Hedgecock et al., 1983; Ou et al., 2010; Sulston and Horvitz, 1977).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ellis and Horvitz, 1986; Hedgecock et al., 1983; Ou et al., 2010; Sulston and Horvitz, 1977.

claim: During the first larval stage, Q neuroblasts on the left (QL) and right (QR) undergo three rounds of asymmetric divisions, which produce three different neurons and two apoptotic cells (Q.aa and Q.pp), respectively.
source: During the first larval stage, Q neuroblasts on the left (QL) and right (QR) undergo three rounds of asymmetric divisions, which produce three different neurons and two apoptotic cells (Q.aa and Q.pp), respectively (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A showing the Q neuroblast lineage.

claim: GFP-tagged NuRD subunits, including HDA-1, LIN-53, CHD-3, and MEP-1, were enriched asymmetrically in the surviving QR.ap cell during QR.a division.
source: We found that GFP-tagged NuRD subunits, including the histone deacetylase HDA-1, the histone binding protein LIN-53, the nucleosome remodeling factor CHD-3, and the MEP-1 protein, were enriched asymmetrically in the surviving QR.ap cell during QR.a division (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: NuRD asymmetric distribution occurred within several minutes after metaphase.
source: Notably, NuRD asymmetric distribution occurred within several minutes after metaphase, while GFP protein translation and chromophore maturation require approximately 30 min in Q neuroblast (Ou and Vale, 2009), suggesting that the asymmetric enrichment of NuRD is likely the result of protein redistribution.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data and comparison with known GFP maturation kinetics.

claim: GFP protein translation and chromophore maturation require approximately 30 min in Q neuroblast.
source: Notably, NuRD asymmetric distribution occurred within several minutes after metaphase, while GFP protein translation and chromophore maturation require approximately 30 min in Q neuroblast (Ou and Vale, 2009), suggesting that the asymmetric enrichment of NuRD is likely the result of protein redistribution.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ou and Vale, 2009.

claim: The asymmetric enrichment of NuRD is likely the result of protein redistribution.
source: Notably, NuRD asymmetric distribution occurred within several minutes after metaphase, while GFP protein translation and chromophore maturation require approximately 30 min in Q neuroblast (Ou and Vale, 2009), suggesting that the asymmetric enrichment of NuRD is likely the result of protein redistribution.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the timing of NuRD asymmetry relative to GFP maturation kinetics.

claim: Nuclear HDA-1 and LIN-53 were released into the cytoplasm and evenly distributed until metaphase in QR.a cells.
source: In QR.a cells, nuclear HDA-1 and LIN-53 were released into the cytoplasm and evenly distributed until metaphase (Figure 1D, Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1D and Videos 3 and 4.

claim: At anaphase, HDA-1 and LIN-53 became enriched in the posterior part of QR.a but became less detectable in the anterior part.
source: At anaphase, HDA-1 and LIN-53 became enriched in the posterior part of QR.a but became less detectable in the anterior part (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B, Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B, and Videos 3 and 4.

claim: Nuclear HDA-1 asymmetry gradually increased from 1.1-fold at anaphase onset to 1.5-fold upon completion of cytokinesis.
source: We quantified the fluorescence intensity ratio between the posterior and anterior chromatids of QR.a, and between QR.ap and QR.aa nuclei, and found that nuclear HDA-1 or LIN-53 asymmetry gradually increased from 1.1-fold at anaphase onset to 1.5- or 1.8-fold upon completion of cytokinesis, respectively (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: Nuclear LIN-53 asymmetry gradually increased from 1.1-fold at anaphase onset to 1.8-fold upon completion of cytokinesis.
source: We quantified the fluorescence intensity ratio between the posterior and anterior chromatids of QR.a, and between QR.ap and QR.aa nuclei, and found that nuclear HDA-1 or LIN-53 asymmetry gradually increased from 1.1-fold at anaphase onset to 1.5- or 1.8-fold upon completion of cytokinesis, respectively (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: NuRD asymmetry became evident at ~4 min and reached a plateau at ~6 min after the anaphase onset.
source: NuRD asymmetry became evident at ~4 min and reached a plateau at ~6 min after the anaphase onset (Figure 1D and F, Figure 1—figure supplements 3A and 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-course fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 1D and F, Figure 1—figure supplements 3A and 4B.

claim: QR.a cell spends ~6 min from anaphase to the completion of cytokinesis.
source: QR.a spent ~6 min from anaphase to the completion of cytokinesis (Chai et al., 2012; Ou et al., 2010), suggesting that QR.a cell establishes NuRD asymmetry during ACD.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chai et al., 2012; Ou et al., 2010.

claim: QR.a cell establishes NuRD asymmetry during ACD.
source: QR.a spent ~6 min from anaphase to the completion of cytokinesis (Chai et al., 2012; Ou et al., 2010), suggesting that QR.a cell establishes NuRD asymmetry during ACD.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the timing of NuRD asymmetry establishment relative to the duration of cell division.

claim: Dynamic and progressively developing NuRD asymmetry was observed in the QL.a, QR.p, and QL.p cell lineages, which generate apoptotic cells.
source: Similar to QR.a, the dynamic and progressively developing NuRD asymmetry was also observed in the QL.a, QR.p, and QL.p cell lineages, which generate apoptotic cells (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplements 3B and 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplements 3B and 4B.

claim: An even distribution of HDA-1 and LIN-53 was observed in two surviving daughters of QR, QL, QL.pa and QR.pa cells, which generate two viable siblings.
source: In contrast, an even distribution of HDA-1 and LIN-53 was observed in two surviving daughters of QR, QL, QL.pa and QR.pa cells, which generate two viable siblings (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The total fluorescence of HDA-1, LIN-53, and MYS-1 remained constant during ACDs.
source: The total fluorescence of HDA-1, LIN-53, and MYS-1 remained constant during ACDs, suggesting that protein redistribution may establish NuRD asymmetry (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4C.

claim: Protein redistribution may establish NuRD asymmetry.
source: The total fluorescence of HDA-1, LIN-53, and MYS-1 remained constant during ACDs, suggesting that protein redistribution may establish NuRD asymmetry (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that total fluorescence remains constant.

claim: Inhibition of PIG-1 kinase led to symmetric Q cell divisions, producing extra neurons derived from some of their apoptotic daughters.
source: Inhibition of a PAR-1 family kinase PIG-1 led to symmetric Q cell divisions, producing extra neurons derived from some of their apoptotic daughters (Cordes et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cordes et al., 2006.

claim: In pig-1 (gm344) mutants, HDA-1 and LIN-53 were evenly partitioned during ACDs.
source: In pig-1 (gm344) mutants, HDA-1 and LIN-53 were evenly partitioned during ACDs (Figure 1—figure supplement 5, Videos 6 and 7), indicating that asymmetric NuRD segregation depends on the PIG-1 kinase.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5 and Videos 6 and 7.

claim: Asymmetric NuRD segregation depends on the PIG-1 kinase.
source: In pig-1 (gm344) mutants, HDA-1 and LIN-53 were evenly partitioned during ACDs (Figure 1—figure supplement 5, Videos 6 and 7), indicating that asymmetric NuRD segregation depends on the PIG-1 kinase.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that NuRD asymmetry is lost in pig-1 mutants.

claim: In 15 out of 17 embryonic ACDs that produce apoptotic daughter cells, the surviving daughter cells showed enrichment of HDA-1 and LIN-53, with an average enrichment ratio exceeding 1.5-fold.
source: Our analysis indicated that in 15 out of 17 embryonic ACDs that produce apoptotic daughter cells, the surviving daughter cells showed enrichment of HDA-1 and LIN-53, with an average enrichment ratio exceeding 1.5-fold (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of fluorescence data shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 2.

claim: The enrichment of HDA-1 and LIN-53 in surviving daughter cells reached statistical significance in 6 out of 17 embryonic ACDs.
source: Notably, this enrichment reached statistical significance in 6 out of 17 embryonic ACDs (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The MSpppaa cell lineage's two daughter cells received comparable levels of NuRD, yet its apoptotic daughter cell completes apoptosis approximately 400 min post-division.
source: Intriguingly, the MSpppaa cell lineage's two daughter cells received comparable levels of NuRD, yet its apoptotic daughter cell completes apoptosis approximately 400 min post-division (Hsieh et al., 2012; Sulston et al., 1983), supporting the hypothesis that lower NuRD concentrations might promote apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Hsieh et al., 2012; Sulston et al., 1983.

claim: Lower NuRD concentrations might promote apoptosis.
source: Intriguingly, the MSpppaa cell lineage's two daughter cells received comparable levels of NuRD, yet its apoptotic daughter cell completes apoptosis approximately 400 min post-division (Hsieh et al., 2012; Sulston et al., 1983), supporting the hypothesis that lower NuRD concentrations might promote apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is a hypothesis supported by the observation that cells with lower NuRD undergo apoptosis.

claim: The apoptotic daughter cell of ABaraaaap completes apoptosis within 35 min.
source: Conversely, the apoptotic daughter cell of ABaraaaap completes apoptosis within 35 min (Sulston et al., 1983), despite receiving a similar amount of NuRD as its non-apoptotic sibling.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sulston et al., 1983.

claim: The regulation of apoptosis in certain embryonic cells appears to be governed by NuRD-independent mechanisms.
source: Therefore, while the regulation of apoptosis in certain embryonic cells appears to be governed by NuRD-independent mechanisms, NuRD asymmetric segregation is evident in several embryonic cell lineages.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that some cells undergo apoptosis despite having similar NuRD levels.

claim: NuRD asymmetric segregation is evident in several embryonic cell lineages.
source: Therefore, while the regulation of apoptosis in certain embryonic cells appears to be governed by NuRD-independent mechanisms, NuRD asymmetric segregation is evident in several embryonic cell lineages.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing NuRD asymmetry in multiple embryonic lineages.

claim: RNAi of hda-1 or lin-53 caused embryonic lethality.
source: As reported before, RNAi of either hda-1 or lin-53 caused embryonic lethality (Shi and Mello, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shi and Mello, 1998.

claim: RNAi of lin-53 led to embryos arrested at gastrulation stage before the generation of apoptotic cells.
source: RNAi of lin-53 led to embryos arrested at gastrulation stage before the generation of apoptotic cells, preventing us from analyzing its roles in somatic apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: hda-1 RNAi embryos arrested between the late gastrulation stage and bean stage.
source: In contrast, hda-1 RNAi embryos arrested between the late gastrulation stage and bean stage, allowing us to tracked some of apoptotic events.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: The sAnxV::GFP sensor labeled an average of 10 cells in ced-1(e1735) mutant embryos treated with control RNAi.
source: The sAnxV::GFP labeled an average of 10 cells in ced-1(e1735) mutant embryos treated with control RNAi and an average of 14 cells in ced-1(e1735); hda-1 RNAi embryos (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The sAnxV::GFP sensor labeled an average of 14 cells in ced-1(e1735); hda-1 RNAi embryos.
source: The sAnxV::GFP labeled an average of 10 cells in ced-1(e1735) mutant embryos treated with control RNAi and an average of 14 cells in ced-1(e1735); hda-1 RNAi embryos (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: RNAi of hda-1 in ced-3, ced-4, ced-9, and egl-1 mutant embryos only generated 0–2 exPS-positive cells.
source: RNAi of hda-1 in these embryos only generated 0–2 exPS-positive cells (Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), indicating that the ectopic increase of apoptosis by HDA-1 inhibition requires the EGL-1-CED-9-CED-4-CED-3 pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The ectopic increase of apoptosis by HDA-1 inhibition requires the EGL-1-CED-9-CED-4-CED-3 pathway.
source: RNAi of hda-1 in these embryos only generated 0–2 exPS-positive cells (Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), indicating that the ectopic increase of apoptosis by HDA-1 inhibition requires the EGL-1-CED-9-CED-4-CED-3 pathway.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that apoptosis pathway mutants suppress the hda-1 RNAi phenotype.

claim: The egl-1 gene was among the upregulated genes in both hda-1 RNAi and lin-53 RNAi conditions.
source: Notably, we found that the apoptosis-inducing gene egl-1 was among the upregulated genes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: egl-1 transcripts were more abundant in hda-1 RNAi and lin-53 RNAi embryos than in control RNAi embryos.
source: Our quantitative RT-PCR results further confirmed that egl-1 transcripts were more abundant in hda-1 RNAi and lin-53 RNAi embryos than in control RNAi embryos (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: RNAi of hda-1 or lin-53 caused an increased number of Pegl-1::NLS::GFP-positive cells.
source: We found that RNAi of hda-1 or lin-53 caused an increased number of Pegl-1::NLS::GFP-positive cells (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The loss of NuRD abnormally activates the egl-1 gene expression.
source: These results indicate that the loss of NuRD abnormally activates the egl-1 gene expression.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that NuRD RNAi increases egl-1 expression.

claim: The transcription start site (TSS) and the gene body region of egl-1 had higher levels of H3K27ac in hda-1 or lin-53 RNAi embryos compared to WT.
source: To test this, we performed ChIP-seq experiments with the anti-H3K27ac antibody and found that the transcription start site (TSS) and the gene body region of egl-1 had higher levels of H3K27ac in hda-1 or lin-53 RNAi embryos compared to WT, while the H3K27ac levels of genes adjacent to egl-1 showed no significant changes (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The H3K27ac levels of genes adjacent to egl-1 showed no significant changes in hda-1 or lin-53 RNAi embryos.
source: To test this, we performed ChIP-seq experiments with the anti-H3K27ac antibody and found that the transcription start site (TSS) and the gene body region of egl-1 had higher levels of H3K27ac in hda-1 or lin-53 RNAi embryos compared to WT, while the H3K27ac levels of genes adjacent to egl-1 showed no significant changes (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: ChIP-qPCR in hda-1 RNAi embryos supported the increased H3K27ac levels at the egl-1 locus.
source: This was supported by ChIP-qPCR in hda-1 RNAi embryos (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Inhibiting NuRD increased the H3K27ac levels at the egl-1 locus, leading to its upregulation and subsequent activation of apoptosis.
source: Therefore, inhibiting NuRD increased the H3K27ac levels at the egl-1 locus, leading to its upregulation and subsequent activation of apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the combined observations of increased H3K27ac, increased egl-1 expression, and increased apoptosis upon NuRD inhibition.

claim: Co-immunoprecipitation and MS with HDA-1::GFP identified 12 subunits of the vacuolar-type H+-ATPase (V-ATPase).
source: Interestingly, our co-immunoprecipitation and MS with HDA-1::GFP identified 12 subunits of the vacuolar-type H+-ATPase (V-ATPase) (Figure 4A and B), consistent with a previous report that used FLAG-tagged LIN-53 to identify 4 V-ATPase subunits (Müthel et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: A previous report using FLAG-tagged LIN-53 identified 4 V-ATPase subunits.
source: Interestingly, our co-immunoprecipitation and MS with HDA-1::GFP identified 12 subunits of the vacuolar-type H+-ATPase (V-ATPase) (Figure 4A and B), consistent with a previous report that used FLAG-tagged LIN-53 to identify 4 V-ATPase subunits (Müthel et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Müthel et al., 2019.

claim: The binding of HDA-1 to V-ATPase subunits in C. elegans was confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation and western blot analysis with anti-V1A/VHA-13 antibodies.
source: We further confirmed the binding of HDA-1 to V-ATPase subunits in C. elegans by co-immunoprecipitation and western blot analysis with anti-V1A/VHA-13 antibodies (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP and western blot data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: V-ATPase is a proton pump that comprises a transmembrane domain (V0) responsible for proton transport across membranes and a peripheral ATP-hydrolytic domain (V1) that catalyzes ATP hydrolysis.
source: V-ATPase is a proton pump that comprises a transmembrane domain (V0) responsible for proton transport across membranes and a peripheral ATP-hydrolytic domain (V1) that catalyzes ATP hydrolysis (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about V-ATPase structure and function.

claim: V-ATPases play a critical role in intracellular pH homeostasis and regulate numerous physiological processes, including apoptosis.
source: V-ATPases play a critical role in intracellular pH homeostasis and regulate numerous physiological processes, including apoptosis (Abbas et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2022; Ernstrom et al., 2012; Vasanthakumar and Rubinstein, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Abbas et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2022; Ernstrom et al., 2012; Vasanthakumar and Rubinstein, 2020.

claim: In DMSO-treated animals, the pHlourin fluorescence intensity remained constant in the posterior portion that forms QR.ap but was significantly reduced in the anterior portion that forms QR.aa.
source: In DMSO-treated animals, the pHlourin fluorescence intensity remained constant in the posterior portion that forms QR.ap but was significantly reduced in the anterior portion that forms QR.aa, indicating that the cytoplasm of the future apoptotic cell became more acidic (Figure 5A and B, Video 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by pHluorin fluorescence data shown in Figure 5A and B, Video 8.

claim: The cytoplasm of the future apoptotic cell became more acidic.
source: In DMSO-treated animals, the pHlourin fluorescence intensity remained constant in the posterior portion that forms QR.ap but was significantly reduced in the anterior portion that forms QR.aa, indicating that the cytoplasm of the future apoptotic cell became more acidic (Figure 5A and B, Video 8).
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the pHluorin fluorescence data.

claim: Cytosolic acidification is a common feature of both death receptor-mediated and mitochondria-dependent apoptosis.
source: This observation is consistent with the recognition that cytosolic acidification is a common feature of both death receptor-mediated and mitochondria-dependent apoptosis (Lagadic-Gossmann et al., 2004; Matsuyama et al., 2000; Matsuyama and Reed, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lagadic-Gossmann et al., 2004; Matsuyama et al., 2000; Matsuyama and Reed, 2000.

claim: BafA1 treatment reduced the pHluorin fluorescence intensity ratio between QR.ap and QR.aa from 1.6-fold to 1.3-fold.
source: Notably, BafA1 treatment reduced the pHluorin fluorescence intensity ratio between QR.ap and QR.aa from 1.6-fold to 1.3-fold (Figure 5A and B, Video 8), suggesting that BafA1 may disrupt the cytosolic pH asymmetry in dividing QR.a cells by inhibiting V-ATPase activity, although we cannot exclude the possibility that the changes in fluorescence could be due to changes in the amount of pHluorin protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative pHluorin fluorescence data shown in Figure 5A and B, Video 8.

claim: BafA1 may disrupt the cytosolic pH asymmetry in dividing QR.a cells by inhibiting V-ATPase activity.
source: Notably, BafA1 treatment reduced the pHluorin fluorescence intensity ratio between QR.ap and QR.aa from 1.6-fold to 1.3-fold (Figure 5A and B, Video 8), suggesting that BafA1 may disrupt the cytosolic pH asymmetry in dividing QR.a cells by inhibiting V-ATPase activity, although we cannot exclude the possibility that the changes in fluorescence could be due to changes in the amount of pHluorin protein.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observed effect of BafA1 on pH asymmetry.

claim: BafA1 treatment resulted in the symmetric segregation of HDA-1 during QR.a division.

claim: The reduced level of NuRD in the apoptotic daughter cell leads to an increased level of H3K27ac at the egl-1 locus.
source: Specifically, we have provided evidence that the reduced level of NuRD in the apoptotic daughter cell leads to an increased level of H3K27ac, an epigenetic modification known to be associated with active gene expression, at the egl-1 locus, resulting in the upregulation of egl-1 expression and subsequent induction of apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the combined observations from NuRD asymmetry, NuRD RNAi effects on H3K27ac and egl-1 expression.

claim: H3K27ac is an epigenetic modification known to be associated with active gene expression.

claim: Increased H3K27ac at the egl-1 locus results in the upregulation of egl-1 expression and subsequent induction of apoptosis.

claim: V-ATPase interacts with NuRD, both of which are asymmetrically segregated into the surviving cell.
source: Based on our results, we propose a dual-function model of V-ATPase in NuRD asymmetric segregation: (i) V-ATPase interacts with NuRD, both of which are asymmetrically segregated into the surviving cell; (ii) the asymmetrical activity of V-ATPase generates a more acidic cytoplasmic environment in the future apoptotic cell portion compared to the surviving portion, which might contribute to the asymmetric segregation of V-ATPase and NuRD.
evidence: This claim is part of a proposed model based on experimental data.

claim: The asymmetrical activity of V-ATPase generates a more acidic cytoplasmic environment in the future apoptotic cell portion compared to the surviving portion.

claim: The more acidic cytoplasmic environment in the future apoptotic cell might contribute to the asymmetric segregation of V-ATPase and NuRD.

claim: Little is known about the asymmetric segregation of epigenetic modification enzymes during ACDs.
source: Despite this, little is known about the asymmetric segregation of epigenetic modification enzymes during ACDs, nor the functions of polarized V-ATPase distribution and cytoplasmic proton asymmetry during this process.

claim: V-ATPase subunits are synthesized and assembled on the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
source: Although V-ATPase is primarily known for its localization and function in the late endosome and lysosome, recent evidence suggests that V-ATPase subunits are synthesized and assembled on the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (Abbas et al., 2020; Graham et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Abbas et al., 2020; Graham et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2020.

claim: V-ATPase colocalizes with the ER marker during ACDs.
source: Our findings demonstrate that V-ATPase colocalizes with the ER marker during ACDs, suggesting that NuRD-V-ATPase may be delivered as cargo on the ER or ER-derived vesicles (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: NuRD-V-ATPase may be delivered as cargo on the ER or ER-derived vesicles.

claim: A polarized microtubule transportation system, governed by specific motor proteins and the microtubule tracks, is responsible for the asymmetric segregation of signaling endosomes during ACDs of Drosophila sensory organ precursors.
source: As reported in previous studies, a polarized microtubule transportation system, governed by specific motor proteins and the microtubule tracks, is responsible for the asymmetric segregation of signaling endosomes during ACDs of Drosophila sensory organ precursors (Derivery et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Derivery et al., 2015.

claim: A similar biased transportation system may play a role in the asymmetric segregation of NuRD-V-ATPase-containing organelles.

evidence: This claim is speculative, based on analogy to other systems.

claim: The NuRD asymmetry on chromosomes (1.5–1.8-fold between QR.ap and QR.aa nuclei) is greater than that between the two daughter cells (approximately 1.3-fold).

claim: The observation of asymmetric segregation of the NuRD complex during cell divisions suggests that the mother cell may play a role in initiating the fate specification of its daughter cells.

claim: In the embryonic cerebral cortex of mammals, approximately 30% of newborn cells undergo programmed cell death.
source: In the embryonic cerebral cortex of mammals, approximately 30% of newborn cells undergo programmed cell death (Voiculescu et al., 2000), which is a significantly higher rate than that observed in C. elegans where only 12% of somatically born cells undergo apoptosis (131 apoptotic cells among 1090 somatically born cells).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Voiculescu et al., 2000.
